claim: Multicellular organisms have evolved from a unicellular ancestor at least 25 times.
source_text: Multicellular organisms have evolved from a unicellular ancestor at least 25 times (Grosberg and Strathmann, 2007)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Grosberg and Strathmann, 2007.

claim: Over 95% of invertase enzyme remains in the cell wall of Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
source_text: Over 95% of this enzyme remains in the cell wall (Esmon et al., 1987; Tammi et al., 1987)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Esmon et al., 1987 and Tammi et al., 1987.

claim: Lab yeast strains cannot grow from low density in low concentrations of sucrose because of diffusion.
source_text: Lab yeast strains cannot grow from low density in low concentrations of sucrose because of diffusion: each cell captures only a small fraction of the sugars that sucrose hydrolysis releases, and the molecules released by other, distant cells are at very low concentration.
evidence_reasoning: This claim draws on established understanding of diffusion and is inferred from the physical properties of sugar molecules in solution.

claim: Forming multicellular clumps overcomes the failure to grow in low sucrose concentrations.
source_text: Forming multicellular clumps overcomes this failure; cells in a clump can capture glucose and fructose diffusing from their neighbors and grow in concentrations of sucrose where low concentrations of individual cells cannot.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on inference from physical principles and is supported by previous work (referenced in the manuscript).

claim: Three engineered strategies allow yeast cells to grow on low sucrose: forming multicellular clumps, importing sucrose before hydrolyzing it, and increasing invertase expression.
source_text: We engineered and tested three strategies that allow yeast cells to grow on low sucrose: forming multicellular clumps, importing sucrose before hydrolyzing it, and increasing invertase expression.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figures 1 and 2 and Table 1.

claim: All but one of the 12 clones selected from 10 independent populations form multicellular clumps as a result of incomplete cell separation.
source_text: All but one of the 12 clones selected from 10 independent populations form multicellular clumps as a result of incomplete cell separation
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations and data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: 10 of the evolved clones elevated invertase expression.
source_text: 10 of the clones elevated invertase expression
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Table 2.

claim: 11 of the evolved clones increased hexose transporter expression.
source_text: 11 increased hexose transporter expression, a strategy we had not engineered
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Table 2.

claim: None of the evolved clones imported sucrose.
source_text: none imported sucrose
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data in Table 4 showing that removal of invertase secretion severely reduced fitness.

claim: Strong expression of secreted invertase allows growth from a single cell at low sucrose concentrations.
source_text: Strong expression of secreted invertase allows growth from a single cell at low sucrose concentrations.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Sucrose import allows growth from a single cell in low sucrose concentrations.
source_text: Sucrose import allows growth from a single cell in low sucrose concentrations.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The three engineered strains all outcompeted the ancestral wild-type lab strain in 1 mM sucrose.
source_text: The three engineered strains all outcompeted the ancestral wild-type lab strain in 1 mM sucrose (Table 1)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by competition experiment data presented in Table 1.

claim: The strain engineered to express increased invertase (EngHiInvertase) was a much worse competitor than the other two engineered strains.
source_text: although the strain engineered to express increased invertase (EngHiInvertase) was a much worse competitor than the other two (EngClumpy, EngSucImport).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by competition data in Table 1.

claim: Ten independent populations of budding yeast were serially diluted in minimal, 1 mM sucrose-containing medium for experimental evolution.
source_text: Ten independent populations of budding yeast were serially diluted in minimal, 1 mM sucrose-containing medium.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the experimental procedure performed by the authors.

claim: Each of the evolved clones strongly outcompeted their ancestor, eliminating it from cultures within two passages on 1 mM sucrose.
source_text: Each of the evolved clones strongly outcompeted their ancestor, eliminating it from cultures within two passages on 1 mM sucrose (Table 1).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by competition experiment data in Table 1.

claim: Efficient use of public goods, liberated through extracellular hydrolysis, selects for the evolution of undifferentiated multicellularity.
source_text: We conclude that efficient use of public goods, liberated through extracellular hydrolysis, selects for the evolution of undifferentiated multicellularity.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental evolution data showing that 11 of 12 clones evolved multicellularity.

claim: All the multicellular clones form clumps as a result of incomplete separation; each clump contains cells of only one color.
source_text: All the multicellular clones are the result of incomplete separation; each clump contains cells of only one or the other color.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 4.

claim: In 10 of the 12 clones invertase (SUC2) expression was elevated between 3- and 21-fold above their ancestor.
source_text: In 10 of the 12 clones invertase (SUC2) expression was elevated between 3- and 21-fold above their ancestor (Table 2)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Table 2.

claim: Hexose transporter expression was elevated in 11 of 12 evolved clones.
source_text: RNA sequencing revealed another change that likely led to better growth in 1 mM sucrose: hexose transporter expression was elevated in 11 of 12 evolved clones.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Table 2.

claim: The expression of HXT4, which encodes a high-affinity glucose transporter, was elevated in 10 of the evolved clones.
source_text: The expression of HXT4, which encodes a high-affinity glucose transporter, was elevated in 10 of these evolved clones (Table 2)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data in Table 2.

claim: Four genes involved in cell separation, AMN1, CTS1, DSE2, and SCW11, had significantly reduced levels in all 11 clumpy evolved clones.
source_text: Four genes involved in cell separation, AMN1, CTS1, DSE2, and SCW11, had significantly reduced levels in all 11 clumpy evolved clones
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Table 3.

claim: Growth of all the evolved clones depends on secreted invertase.
source_text: In each case, the evolved clone quickly outcompeted the version that did not secrete invertase (Table 4), demonstrating that growth of all the evolved clones depends on secreted invertase.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by competition experiments shown in Table 4.

claim: Each evolved clone quickly outcompeted the ancestor in low sucrose and lost to its ancestor in high glucose.
source_text: Each evolved clone quickly outcompeted the ancestor in low sucrose and lost to its ancestor in high glucose (Table 1).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by competition data in Table 1.

claim: Four of the evolved clones also lost quickly on low monosaccharide; the remaining clones had approximately the same fitness as the ancestor.
source_text: Four of the evolved clones also lost quickly on low monosaccharide; the remaining clones had approximately the same fitness as the ancestor
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by competition data in Table 1.

claim: Bulk segregant analysis uses sexual reproduction to separate causal from hitchhiking mutations.
source_text: To identify the causal mutations, we used bulk segregant analysis, which uses sexual reproduction to separate causal from hitchhiking mutations.
evidence_reasoning: This describes an established method in genetics, supported by citations in the text.

claim: Over all 12 clones, the 80 putative causal mutations lie in or near 53 genes.
source_text: Over all 12 clones, the 80 putative causal mutations lie in or near 53 genes.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on whole genome sequencing and bulk segregant analysis data presented in Table 5.

claim: Two genes, ACE2 and UBR1, were mutated in at least half the clones.
source_text: Two genes, ACE2 and UBR1, were mutated in at least half the clones
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by sequencing data presented in Table 5.

claim: ACE2 was mutated in eight evolved clones; six of these mutations were nonsense mutations.
source_text: ACE2 was mutated in eight evolved clones; six of these mutations were nonsense mutations scattered through the open reading frame.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by sequencing data in Table 5.

claim: Ace2 activates the transcription of enzymes that degrade the septum that connects mother to daughter cell.
source_text: Ace2 activates the transcription of enzymes that degrade the septum that connects mother to daughter cell (Colman-Lerner et al., 2001; Sbia et al., 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: UBR1 was mutated in 6 of the 12 clones; four mutations were nonsense mutations.
source_text: UBR1 was mutated in 6 of the 12 clones; four mutations were nonsense mutations
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by sequencing data in Table 5.

claim: Ubr1 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase in the N-end rule pathway.
source_text: Ubr1 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase in the N-end rule pathway. Ubr1 targets proteins with certain N-terminal amino acids, which are exposed by proteolytic cleavage or removal of the N-terminal methionine, for degradation (Bartel et al., 1990).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Bartel et al., 1990.

claim: One of the genes in the Rgt1 pathway was mutated in 8 of the 12 clones.
source_text: One of the genes in the Rgt1 pathway was mutated in 8 of the 12 clones: SNF3 (3 missense), MTH1 (2 nonsense), and RGT1 (2 nonsense, 1 missense)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by sequencing data in Table 5.

claim: The Rgt1 pathway controls cells' response to external glucose concentrations.
source_text: The Rgt1 pathway controls cells' response to external glucose concentrations. In high glucose, Rgt1, a transcription factor, represses the expression of high affinity hexose transporters such as HXT4 (Ozcan and Johnston, 1999).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Ozcan and Johnston, 1999.

claim: IRA1 or IRA2 were mutated in four unrelated evolved clones.
source_text: IRA1 or IRA2 were mutated in four unrelated evolved clones (3 missense, 1 nonsense).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by sequencing data in Table 5.

claim: Mutations were found in four of the at least 20 proteins that make up Mediator: SIN4, CSE2, MED1, and NUT1.
source_text: We found mutations in four of the at least 20 proteins that make up Mediator (Myers and Kornberg, 2000): SIN4 (2 missense mutations), CSE2 (1 nonsense mutation), MED1 (1 nonsense mutation), and NUT1 (1 nonsense mutation).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by sequencing data in Table 5.

claim: Both the evolved and recreated clones outcompeted their ancestor in 1–2 passages.
source_text: Both the evolved and recreated clones outcompeted their ancestor in 1–2 passages (Table 1) showing that they are much fitter on low sucrose.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by competition data in Table 1.

claim: Both recreated strains were slightly less fit than their evolved counterparts.
source_text: Both recreated strains were slightly less fit their evolved counterparts: there were fewer recreated than evolved cells after six passages (46 generations).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by competition data in Table 1.

claim: All five mutations in Recreated2 were strongly selected for.
source_text: All five mutations in Recreated2 were strongly selected for
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by bulk segregant analysis data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Six of the eight mutations in Recreated9 were strongly selected for.
source_text: six of the eight mutations in Recreated9 were strongly selected for
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by bulk segregant analysis data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Several mutations were selected for in low sucrose but not in low monosaccharide: mutations in MTH1, CSE2, and ACE2 in Recreated2; and in MCK1, IRC8, and GIN4 in Recreated9.
source_text: Several mutations were selected for in low sucrose but not in low monosaccharide: mutations in MTH1, CSE2, and ACE2 in Recreated2; and in MCK1, IRC8, and GIN4 in Recreated9.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by bulk segregant analysis data shown in Figure 8.

claim: An ace2Δ strain is morphologically similar to EvoClone2.
source_text: an ace2Δ strain is morphologically similar to EvoClone2
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: A mck1-G227Vfs249 irc8-G57V gin4-W19* strain is morphologically similar to EvoClone9.
source_text: a mck1-G227Vfs249 irc8-G57V gin4-W19* strain is morphologically similar to EvoClone9
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Multicellular clumps were specifically selected by growth in low sucrose, rather than being a general response to low sugar concentrations.
source_text: This shows that multicellular clumps were specifically selected by growth in low sucrose, rather than being a general response to low sugar concentrations.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from competition and bulk segregant analysis data showing differential selection in sucrose vs. monosaccharide.

claim: Clumpiness alone was not sufficient to match the growth of the evolved strains in sucrose.
source_text: But clumpiness alone was not sufficient to match the growth of the evolved strains in sucrose—the engineered clumpy strain (EngClumpy) was not as fit in 1 mM sucrose as one of the evolved clones that had similar clump size (EvoClone2) (Table 1).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by competition data in Table 1.

claim: The increase in HXT4 expression is a result of the MTH1 loss of function mutation (mth1-H154Tfs156).
source_text: The increase in HXT4 expression is clearly a result of the MTH1 loss of function mutation (mth1-H154Tfs156): all combinations containing this allele have higher HXT4 expression than those containing the ancestral MTH1 allele.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: SUC2 expression is a complex phenotype, which is under the quantitative control of alleles at several genes.
source_text: The gradient in SUC2 expression across the allelic combinations indicates that SUC2 expression is a complex phenotype, which is under the quantitative control alleles at several genes.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from RT-qPCR data showing gradual changes in SUC2 expression across different allelic combinations.

claim: The clumpiness in EvoClone2 is caused by the loss of function mutation in ACE2.
source_text: This result confirms that the clumpiness in EvoClone2 is caused by the loss of function mutation in ACE2.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by microscopy observations of strains with different ACE2 alleles.

claim: A loss of function mutation in ACE2 was likely the primary contributor to the clumpy phenotype in at least 6 of the 11 multicellular clones.
source_text: A loss of function mutation in ACE2 was likely the primary contributor to the clumpy phenotype in at least 6 of the 11 multicellular clones.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from sequencing data showing ACE2 mutations in 6 clones and the known function of ACE2.

claim: None of the clones became clumpy by restoring function to AMN1.
source_text: None of our clones became clumpy by restoring function to AMN1, the gene whose loss of function allele was selected for during laboratory domestication of budding yeast (Yvert et al., 2003).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on sequencing data showing no AMN1 mutations and cites previous work on AMN1.

claim: Increasing invertase expression will increase the rate of sucrose hydrolysis at the cell wall.
source_text: Increased invertase expression will increase the rate of sucrose hydrolysis at the cell wall.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from basic biochemical principles about enzyme kinetics.

claim: Making more hexose transporters will increase the fraction of the monosaccharides that are imported rather than escaping to the bulk medium.
source_text: making more hexose transporters will increase the fraction of the monosaccharides that are imported rather than escaping to the bulk medium
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from basic principles of membrane transport and diffusion.

claim: Increasing invertase expression, making cell clumps, and making more hexose transporters will act together to increase fitness on low sucrose.
source_text: Thus we expect that increasing invertase expression, making cell clumps, and making more hexose transporters will act together to increase fitness on low sucrose.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference from the individual effects of each strategy.

claim: Low extracellular glucose induces the expression of both high affinity hexose transporters and invertase.
source_text: Because low extracellular glucose induces the expression of both high affinity hexose transporters and invertase
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established knowledge of yeast glucose regulation.

claim: Clumps may increase invertase expression because concentrating the cells in space collectively raises the local glucose concentration.
source_text: clumps may increase invertase expression because concentrating the cells in space collectively raises the local glucose concentration
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for the observed correlation between clumping and invertase expression.

claim: Many of the mutations selected are likely to affect the linked processes of sugar harvesting and the control of cell growth.
source_text: Many of the mutations we selected are likely to affect the linked processes of sugar harvesting and the control of cell growth.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the known functions of the mutated genes.

claim: Prevention of N-end rule mediated protein degradation increases the expression of genes that promote growth in carbon limited cells.
source_text: We suspect that prevention of N-end rule mediated protein degradation increases the expression of genes that promote growth in carbon limited cells: in both evolved clones that we recreated, the evolved allele of UBR1 was selected for in sucrose and low monosaccharide and selected against in high glucose
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation based on the selection patterns of UBR1 mutations.

claim: The pattern of mutations in the RGT1 group of genes is consistent with selection to reduce the repression mediated by Rgt1 and Mth1.
source_text: The pattern of mutations we observe in these genes is consistent with selection to reduce the repression mediated by Rgt1 and Mth1.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the types and locations of mutations observed in these genes.

claim: Mutations in IRA1 and IRA2 are likely to reduce the activity of Ira1 and Ira2 and thus increase the activity of Ras at low sugar concentrations, promoting growth.
source_text: Mutations in IRA1 and IRA2 in four independent lineages. These mutations are likely to reduce the activity of Ira1 and Ira2 and thus increase the activity of Ras at low sugar concentrations, promoting growth.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the known function of Ira1 and Ira2 as negative regulators of Ras.

claim: Disruption of either IRA1 or IRA2 increases sensitivity to heat shock.
source_text: Disruption of either IRA1 or IRA2 increases sensitivity to heat shock (Tanaka et al., 1989, 1990).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Tanaka et al., 1989, 1990.

claim: The sharing of public goods was the initial selection for undifferentiated multicellularity.
source_text: The combination of laboratory engineering and evolutionary analysis shown here and in our previous work supports the speculation that the sharing of public goods was the initial selection for undifferentiated multicellularity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental evolution data and previous work.

claim: For organisms with rigid cell walls like yeast, algae, and bacteria, cells must secrete enzymes to separate mother from daughter after cytokinesis.
source_text: For organisms with rigid cell walls like yeast, algae, and bacteria, cells must secrete enzymes to separate mother from daughter after cytokinesis.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established biological knowledge about cell division in walled organisms.

claim: The target size for mutations in cell separation enzymes and their control circuits will be large, making it easy to evolve undifferentiated multicellularity.
source_text: The target size for mutations in these enzymes and the control circuits that regulate their production will be large, making it easy to evolve undifferentiated multicellularity.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that multiple genes control cell separation.

claim: Lab strains of yeast were selected to be unicellular during their domestication.
source_text: Although lab strains of yeast were selected to be unicellular during their domestication (Mortimer and Johnston, 1986)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Mortimer and Johnston, 1986.

claim: The level of clumpiness varies in wild isolates of yeast.
source_text: the level of clumpiness varies in wild isolates of yeast
evidence_reasoning: This is based on general knowledge about yeast diversity.

claim: Undifferentiated multicellularity may have been recurrently selected for its advantage in harvesting nutrients or for protection from stress.
source_text: undifferentiated multicellularity may have been recurrently selected for its advantage in harvesting nutrients or for protection from stress (Smukalla et al., 2008)
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative claim supported by a citation to Smukalla et al., 2008.

claim: Organisms without a cell wall, such as animal cells, would need another innovation, such as cell-adhering cadherins, in order to evolve multicellular clumps.
source_text: Organisms without a cell wall, such as animal cells, would need another innovation, such as cell-adhering cadherins (Abedin and King, 2008), in order to evolve multicellular clumps.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative claim about evolutionary mechanisms, supported by a citation to Abedin and King, 2008.

claim: There is suggestive evidence of undifferentiated eukaryotic multicellularity 2 billion years ago.
source_text: Indeed, there is suggestive evidence of undifferentiated eukaryotic multicellularity 2 billion years ago (El Albani et al. 2010)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to El Albani et al. 2010.

claim: The radiation of more complex multicellularity is not seen for over a billion years after the first evidence of undifferentiated multicellularity.
source_text: but the radiation of more complex multicellularity is not seen for over a billion years later
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established paleontological knowledge.

claim: The effectiveness of clumping as a strategy could be improved if a limited number of cells increase their enzyme secretion.
source_text: From our data, we speculate that the effectiveness of clumping as a strategy could be improved if a limited number of cells increase their enzyme secretion.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference from the experimental data.

claim: Simple division of labor may have been the precursor to complex multicellularity in the lineages that lead to animals and other complex multicellular species.
source_text: Such a simple division of labor may have been the precursor to complex multicellularity in the lineages that lead to animals and other complex multicellular species.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative evolutionary hypothesis.
